$comment: AUTHORITATIVE BOOKING-HORIZON STRATIFICATION POLICY — SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH.
This file defines (a) which advance-purchase horizons are collected and (b) how the
horizon-specific indices are combined into a route index. It is read at runtime by
backend/engine/horizon.py. Nothing else defines horizon weights.
IMPORTANT: the 'expected_price_multiplier' fields that previously lived here were
SIMULATOR CALIBRATION PARAMETERS. They described how the synthetic generator prices
each horizon. They were never a methodological weighting and must never be used as
one -- doing so would make the index reproduce the generator's own configuration.
They have been moved to backend/scraper/sources/simulator.py where they belong, and
the weighting below is stated independently of them.

horizons.label: T+1
horizons.name: One day advance
horizons.statistical_rationale: Captures urgent short-notice demand while avoiding same-day operational edge cases and already-closed inventory.

horizons.label: T+7
horizons.name: One week advance
horizons.statistical_rationale: A common revenue-management threshold at which discount fare buckets close.

horizons.label: T+15
horizons.name: Two week advance
horizons.statistical_rationale: Covers the 14/21-day advance purchase fare classes typical of planned business and early leisure travel.

horizons.label: T+30
horizons.name: One month advance
horizons.statistical_rationale: Planned discretionary leisure travel. Serves as the reference anchor for the advance-purchase curve.

horizons.label: T+45
horizons.name: Forty-five days advance
horizons.statistical_rationale: Captures early planned travel and provides a longer-lead reference point for lead-time elasticity.

weighting.formula: alpha_h = 1 / H for each of the H horizons that has a computable index
why_equal: Ideally alpha_h would be the share of tickets actually SOLD at each advance-purchase
horizon. That distribution is held by airlines and is not published, so it cannot be
Equal weighting is therefore chosen as an explicit, documented, and defensible
convention rather than an estimate. Its key property is that it is FIXED: because the
weights do not depend on how many observations each horizon happens to contribute,
the combined route index cannot move merely because the sample composition shifted.
Pooling observations across horizons (the previous behaviour) does not have this
property: it makes the index sensitive to the horizon mix, because T+1 fares sit at a
structurally higher level than T+45 fares.
weighting.renormalization_policy: If a horizon has no computable index for a period, the remaining horizons are renormalized to sum to 1.0 and the missing horizon is recorded on the index record. The index is only published when at least min_horizons_for_route_index horizons are present.
weighting.upgrade_path: Replace with booking-distribution weights if and when advance-purchase sales shares become available from a citable source. Any such change is a methodology change and must create an index_revisions record.
